analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) Equities Update, 2) Jan Hatzius on Downside Risks to Growth, 3) SGD/INR Carry Idea, 4) NatGas Update and 5) GS FX Webcast Today
key_insights: GS US semis analyst Jim Schneider retains Buy on Nvidia with a 12-month PT of $220 (22x P/E on normalized EPS of $10.00), citing Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO. The multiple is expected to re-rate, though it stays pressured pending reported investigations.

GS trading desk (Privorotsky) saw a massive short squeeze on Huang's return and asks whether the Trump put is back. CoreWeave +22%, Taiwan +9%, TSMC and Foxconn limit up, Kospi +6.5%, Nikkei +4%. China lagged with CSI 300 +0.14% and Hang Seng -0.73% early.

Watch items on chips: whether Commerce grants licenses for Chinese customers to access advanced chips via offshore data centers, and whether Congress builds veto-proof support for tougher chip restrictions. Huang testifies Dec. 1.

Hatzius lists downside risks to the base case of steady global growth in 2027: renewed Iran escalation hitting real income, bond market turbulence in the Euro Area and France ahead of the presidential election, and a sharper AI investment slowdown or larger labour market impact.
France runs a budget deficit of about 5.5% of GDP, which Hatzius describes as far from sustainable.
The 2026 positive wealth effect supported higher-income spending and offset some energy-price drag. Weaker markets in 2027 alongside a major energy shock could hit spending harder.

GS Asia Macro Strats propose a 6m dual digital: buy USDSGD above ATM and USDINR below 2% ITM, costing 14.4% USD, with 30% and 50% individual probabilities and +15% correlation. Max loss is premium paid. It is framed as a leveraged USDINR carry entry.

India equity inflows reached nearly US$12bn in November. Long-only funds were about 175bp underweight India at end-September, and a move to neutral implies roughly US$24bn of inflows. The flow math supports INR unless the RBI absorbs inflows.

India's underlying BOP is about -US$4bn/month before portfolio flows. The RBI letting oil companies source USD directly could remove about US$10bn/month of USD demand. GS expects meaningful RBI dollar buying around 92 once the ~US$13bn NDF short is covered.

GS Commodities: colder NW Europe forecasts pushed TTF to 90 EUR/MWh, up 6% WoW. If the cold shock realizes with no offsets, end-winter NW Europe gas inventories would be only 14% full versus the 20% base case, the lowest since 9% in 2018.

If the rest of winter is average, GS estimates TTF must rally to 106 EUR/MWh to restore inventories near 20%, versus a 65 EUR/MWh 1Q27 base case. Persian Gulf LNG exports fell from over 60% of pre-war levels in early Nov to 25% last week, adding upside risk.
GS FX Webcast on the 2027 FX Outlook is today at 2pm London.

Tighter US chip export restrictions and Congress action.
Renewed Iran escalation and energy shock.

vol_and_positioning: Shorts added into end of week were squeezed on Huang's reinstatement, producing a massive rally in AI-linked equities.
Long-only funds remain about 175bp underweight India as of end-September per GIR, with a return to neutral implying roughly US$24bn of inflows.
The ~US$13bn NDF short in INR is expected to be substantially covered before RBI dollar buying becomes meaningful near 92.
Dual digital structure on USDSGD/USDINR costs 14.4% USD, with individual probabilities of 30% and 50% and +15% correlation.
geopolitical: Renewed escalation in Iran flagged by Hatzius as a downside risk to 2027 growth through real income and an energy shock.
Oil moved lower on headlines of a potentially delayed timeline for geopolitical escalation in the Middle East.
Persian Gulf LNG export flows fell from over 60% of pre-war levels in early Nov to 25% last week.
The administration tightened rules on remote access to advanced chips last week, and Congress may seek tougher restrictions.
French presidential election run-up raises bond market risk.
